title: UGC NET Artificial Intelligence & Data Science Specialized Mock Examination

questions.question_text: In Breadth-First Search, if the branching factor is b and depth of shallowest solution is d, what is the space complexity?
questions.explanation: BFS stores all generated nodes in memory at the current frontier level. At depth d, there are b^d leaf nodes in memory. Hence space complexity is O(b^d).
questions.numerical_formula: Time Complexity of BFS = O(b^d), Space = O(b^d)
questions.real_time_application: GPS Navigation routing in sparse road networks; Web crawler link traversal.

questions.question_text: An A* search algorithm is guaranteed to find an optimal path if the heuristic function h(n) is:
questions.option_b: Admissible and never overestimates the true cost
questions.option_c: Equal to the path cost g(n)
questions.explanation: For tree search, admissibility (h(n) <= h*(n)) is sufficient for optimality. For graph search, consistency (triangle inequality h(n) <= c(n,a,n') + h(n')) guarantees optimal paths without reopening closed nodes.
questions.numerical_formula: f(n) = g(n) + h(n), with h(n) <= h*(n) guaranteeing tree-search optimality.
questions.real_time_application: Warehouse AGV (Automated Guided Vehicle) collision-free shortest path planning.

questions.question_text: What is the primary advantage of Iterative Deepening A* (IDA*) over standard A* search?
questions.option_b: It reduces memory consumption to linear O(bd)
questions.option_c: It does not require a heuristic
questions.option_d: It works only on directed graphs
questions.explanation: A* keeps all explored nodes in memory (exponential O(b^d)), which causes out-of-memory errors on hard problems. IDA* uses depth-first contour cutoffs, reducing memory to O(bd) while retaining optimality.
questions.numerical_formula: Space complexity of IDA* = O(b * d) with f-contour cutoffs.
questions.real_time_application: Embedded robotics pathfinding with strict RAM limits (Microcontroller AI).

questions.question_text: In a two-player zero-sum game with branching factor b and game depth d, the time complexity of the Minimax algorithm is:
questions.explanation: Minimax traverses all states in the complete game tree up to maximum depth d with branching factor b, yielding exact time complexity O(b^d).
questions.numerical_formula: Minimax(s) = max_a Minimax(Result(s,a)) for MAX node; min_a for MIN node.
questions.real_time_application: Chess and Checkers automated engines (Stockfish position evaluation).

questions.question_text: With optimal move ordering, Alpha-Beta pruning reduces the time complexity of minimax from O(b^d) to:
questions.explanation: When child moves are examined in best-first order, Alpha-Beta prunes roughly half the tree branches at alternating depths, achieving O(b^(d/2)) complexity, effectively doubling the search depth.
questions.numerical_formula: Best-case time complexity with optimal ordering = O(b^(d/2)), doubling effective search depth.
questions.real_time_application: Automated high-frequency algorithmic bid-ask auction pricing engines.

questions.question_text: In Simulated Annealing, when the temperature T approaches 0, the algorithm behaves exactly like:
questions.explanation: As T -> 0, the acceptance probability exp(-delta_E / T) for worse moves approaches 0, meaning only strictly improving moves are accepted, reducing to greedy hill climbing.
questions.numerical_formula: Probability of accepting worse state: P = exp(-delta_E / T)
questions.real_time_application: VLSI chip layout gate placement optimization and Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP).

questions.question_text: Which search algorithm combines the linear space complexity of DFS with the completeness of BFS?
questions.explanation: IDDFS runs DFS with incrementally increasing depth limits. It is complete, optimal for uniform step costs, and retains linear space complexity O(bd).
questions.numerical_formula: Branching factor b* calculation: N = 1 + b* + (b*)^2 + ... + (b*)^d
questions.real_time_application: End-to-end autonomous navigation and routing engines.

questions.question_text: The proposition (P -> Q) -> (~P -> ~Q) is a:
questions.explanation: When P=False and Q=True, (P->Q) is True while (~P->~Q) is (True->False) which is False. True->False evaluates to False. When P=True, Q=True, it evaluates to True. Since it is neither always True nor always False, it is a Contingency.
questions.numerical_formula: Implication elimination: (P -> Q) is logically equivalent to (~P v Q).
questions.real_time_application: Hardware circuit verification and SAT solvers for microchip safety checks.

questions.question_text: In Skolemization, an existential quantifier within the scope of universal quantifiers is replaced by:
questions.option_b: A Skolem function of the universally quantified variables
questions.explanation: Because the existential variable depends on the universal variable preceding it, it must be mapped to a function of those universal variables (Skolem function).
questions.numerical_formula: Eliminate existential quantifiers: exists y P(x, y) becomes P(x, f(x)) where f is a Skolem function.
questions.real_time_application: Legal contract verification and regulatory compliance automated rule engines.

questions.question_text: Which substitution represents the Most General Unifier (MGU) for P(x, f(y)) and P(a, f(b))?
questions.explanation: Matching terms pairwise: x unifies with a ({x/a}), and f(y) unifies with f(b) which yields y unifies with b ({y/b}). The combined MGU is {x/a, y/b}.
questions.numerical_formula: Resolvent of (A v B) and (~A v C) with substitution theta is (B v C)theta.
questions.real_time_application: Automated medical diagnosis expert systems (MYCIN inference engine).

questions.question_text: In Frame-based knowledge representation, procedures attached to slots that execute when values are accessed or updated are called:
questions.explanation: In Frame systems, procedural attachments triggered automatically upon slot query or modification are known as demons (such as IF-NEEDED, IF-ADDED, IF-REMOVED).
questions.numerical_formula: Multiple inheritance ambiguity resolved via Topological Sort / Inferential Distance.
questions.real_time_application: Enterprise Knowledge Graphs (Google Knowledge Graph, Wikidata entity linking).

questions.question_text: In a Bayesian Belief Network, the Markov Blanket of a node X consists of:
questions.option_b: Its parents, its children, and the other parents of its children (spouses)
questions.explanation: A node X is conditionally independent of all other nodes in the network given its Markov Blanket, which strictly contains its parents, its children, and its children's co-parents (spouses).
questions.numerical_formula: P(X1, ..., Xn) = Prod_{i=1}^n P(Xi | Parents(Xi))
questions.real_time_application: Credit card fraud detection and spam filtering engines.

questions.question_text: If A is a fuzzy set with membership mu_A(x) = 0.7 and B is a fuzzy set with mu_B(x) = 0.4, the membership value in (A n ~B) is:
questions.explanation: Complement mu_{~B}(x) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6. Intersection is the minimum: min(0.7, 0.6) = 0.6.
questions.numerical_formula: mu_{A n B}(x) = min(mu_A(x), mu_B(x)); mu_{A u B}(x) = max(mu_A(x), mu_B(x))
questions.real_time_application: Automated anti-lock braking systems (ABS) and washing machine load sensors.

questions.question_text: Which defuzzification method calculates the center of gravity of the combined fuzzy output area?
questions.explanation: The Centroid / Center of Gravity (COG) method calculates the center of area under the aggregated fuzzy membership curve, providing the smoothest physical control signal.
questions.numerical_formula: Centroid Defuzzification z* = Integral(z * mu(z) dz) / Integral(mu(z) dz)
questions.real_time_application: High-speed bullet train speed-control actuators and industrial climate controls.

questions.question_text: Which regularization technique promotes feature sparsity by driving irrelevant weights to exactly zero?
questions.explanation: L1 regularization adds the absolute sum of weights to the loss, which has diamond-shaped constraint boundaries that intersect feature axes, forcing uninformative weights to become exactly 0 (sparsity).
questions.numerical_formula: Lasso Cost = MSE + lambda * Sum(|w_i|); Ridge Cost = MSE + lambda * Sum(w_i^2)
questions.real_time_application: Real estate price prediction and customer churn probability estimation.

questions.question_text: In the ID3 algorithm, if a dataset S has 9 positive and 5 negative examples, the entropy Entropy(S) is calculated using:
questions.explanation: Shannon Entropy is defined as -Sum(p_i * log2(p_i)). With p(+) = 9/14 and p(-) = 5/14, Entropy = -(9/14)*log2(9/14) - (5/14)*log2(5/14) approx 0.940 bits.
questions.numerical_formula: Gain(S, A) = Entropy(S) - Sum_{v} (|S_v| / |S|) * Entropy(S_v)
questions.real_time_application: Loan credit approval engines and clinical triage risk classification.

questions.question_text: In Support Vector Machines, if the hyperparameter C is set to an extremely large value, the model will:
questions.option_a: Allow large margins and risk underfitting
questions.option_b: Penalize training errors heavily and risk overfitting
questions.option_d: Convert to a linear regression model
questions.explanation: The hyperparameter C balances margin width against misclassification penalties. A huge C forces zero margin violations on the training set (hard margin behavior), which risks severe overfitting.
questions.numerical_formula: Margin width = 2 / ||w||. Kernel function K(x, z) = exp(-gamma * ||x - z||^2)
questions.real_time_application: Cancer tumor classification from gene expression microarrays.

questions.question_text: In Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering, Single Linkage defines the distance between two clusters as:
questions.option_a: The maximum distance between any two points in the clusters
questions.option_b: The minimum distance between any single point in one cluster and any single point in the other
questions.option_d: The average of all pairwise distances
questions.explanation: Single linkage calculates the minimum distance between points across clusters, which can produce long elongated chaining clusters.
questions.numerical_formula: k-Means objective J = Sum_{i=1}^k Sum_{x in C_i} ||x - mu_i||^2
questions.real_time_application: Customer market segmentation for targeted e-commerce marketing.

questions.question_text: In Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the first principal component corresponds to:
questions.option_a: The eigenvector associated with the smallest eigenvalue
questions.option_b: The eigenvector associated with the largest eigenvalue
questions.option_c: The mean of the feature vector
questions.option_d: The determinant of the covariance matrix
questions.explanation: The first principal component captures the maximum variance in the data, which mathematically corresponds to the eigenvector of the sample covariance matrix that has the largest eigenvalue.
questions.numerical_formula: Principal components are eigenvectors of covariance matrix Sigma = (1/N) * X^T * X
questions.real_time_application: Facial recognition feature compression (Eigenfaces) and financial risk factor analysis.

questions.question_text: Why is the ReLU activation function f(x) = max(0, x) preferred over the Sigmoid function in deep neural networks?
questions.option_a: ReLU is completely bounded between 0 and 1
questions.option_b: ReLU mitigates the vanishing gradient problem for positive inputs
questions.explanation: The derivative of the sigmoid function saturates at 0 for large positive or negative values, causing gradients to vanish during backpropagation in deep architectures. ReLU has a constant derivative of 1 for x > 0.
questions.numerical_formula: delta_j = dE/d(net_j) = (dE/dy_j) * f'(net_j); w_ij = w_ij - eta * delta_j * y_i
questions.real_time_application: Autonomous vehicle computer vision and optical character recognition (OCR).

questions.question_text: An input image of size 32x32 is convolved with a 5x5 kernel using stride S=1 and zero padding P=2. What is the output feature map size?
questions.explanation: Using formula O = floor((W - K + 2P)/S) + 1: O = floor((32 - 5 + 2*2)/1) + 1 = floor(31/1) + 1 = 32. Output is 32x32 ('Same' padding).
questions.numerical_formula: Output Dimension O = floor((W - K + 2P) / S) + 1
questions.real_time_application: Radiology chest X-ray pneumonia detection and biometric facial unlocking.

questions.question_text: In the Transformer attention mechanism, why is the dot product Q * K^T scaled by 1/sqrt(d_k)?
questions.option_a: To convert vectors to unit length
questions.option_b: To prevent extremely large values that push the Softmax function into regions with near-zero gradients
questions.option_c: To eliminate the need for positional encoding
questions.explanation: For large key dimensions d_k, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) stabilizes the gradient flow.
questions.numerical_formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V
questions.real_time_application: Large Language Models (ChatGPT, Claude) and real-time speech translation.

questions.question_text: In TF-IDF scoring, if a word appears in all N documents of a corpus, its IDF value will be:
questions.explanation: IDF is calculated as log(N / DF). If the term appears in all N documents, DF = N, so IDF = log(N / N) = log(1) = 0. Such ubiquitous words receive zero weight.
questions.numerical_formula: TF-IDF(t, d, D) = TF(t, d) * log(N / DF(t))
questions.real_time_application: Legal document discovery, sentiment analysis, and search engine ranking.

questions.question_text: To parse a string of length n using the Cocke-Younger-Kasami (CYK) algorithm, the grammar must first be in:
questions.explanation: The CYK dynamic programming algorithm requires the context-free grammar to be strictly in Chomsky Normal Form (CNF) where all productions are of the form A -> BC or A -> a.
questions.numerical_formula: CYK algorithm time complexity is O(n^3 * |G|), parsing arbitrary CFGs in polynomial time.
questions.real_time_application: Syntax tree analysis in compilers and grammatical structure analysis in Siri/Alexa.

questions.question_text: In the Hadoop MapReduce framework, what operation occurs between the Map phase and the Reduce phase?
questions.explanation: The intermediate key-value pairs produced by Mappers undergo Shuffle and Sort, which aggregates all values associated with the same intermediate key before feeding them to the appropriate Reducer.
questions.numerical_formula: Map: (k1, v1) -> list(k2, v2); Reduce: (k2, list(v2)) -> list(k3, v3)
questions.real_time_application: Large-scale web index creation (Google PageRank computation over billions of URLs).

questions.question_text: Which of the following Apache Spark operations represents a Wide Dependency that triggers a network shuffle across cluster nodes?
questions.explanation: map(), filter(), and flatMap() are Narrow dependencies where each parent partition is used by at most one child partition without network shuffling. groupByKey() requires shuffling data across multiple cluster nodes.
questions.numerical_formula: Wide transformation (e.g., groupByKey, reduceByKey) requires network shuffling across partitions.
questions.real_time_application: Real-time streaming fraud prevention in banking transactions.

questions.question_text: According to Brewer's CAP theorem, in the presence of a network partition, a distributed system must choose between:
questions.explanation: When network partitions inevitably occur (P is mandatory in distributed systems), the architect must choose whether to maintain strong Consistency (rejecting out-of-sync requests) or high Availability (serving stale responses).
questions.numerical_formula: CAP theorem: A distributed network can satisfy at most two of {C, A, P} simultaneously.
questions.real_time_application: Social media graph feeds (Instagram/Twitter follow relationships and timeline generation).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a Type 1 (Bare-Metal) Hypervisor?
questions.explanation: Type 1 Hypervisors run directly on the bare physical host hardware without an underlying host operating system (e.g., VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, Xen). VirtualBox and VMware Workstation run on top of an existing OS (Type 2).
questions.numerical_formula: Container virtualization isolates processes sharing host kernel, achieving sub-second startup.
questions.real_time_application: Cloud microservices auto-scaling on Amazon AWS ECS / Google Cloud Run during flash sales.

questions.question_text: In an imbalanced classification problem where false negatives are catastrophically costly (e.g., rare disease screening), which metric should be maximized?
questions.explanation: Recall = TP / (TP + FN). When false negatives must be minimized (missing a sick patient is disastrous), maximizing Recall ensures as many true positive cases as possible are detected.
questions.numerical_formula: Precision = TP / (TP + FP); Recall = TP / (TP + FN); F1 = 2 * (Prec * Rec) / (Prec + Rec)
questions.real_time_application: Automated medical pathology imaging quality control and fraud classifier monitoring.

questions.question_text: Which learning paradigm allows an agent to learn optimal behaviors by interacting with an environment through trial-and-error rewards?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement Learning formalizes decision-making via Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), where an agent learns an optimal policy through scalar feedback rewards.
questions.numerical_formula: Total Marks = 200; UGC NET JRF target = 65%+ aggregate score.
questions.real_time_application: End-to-end examination readiness and professional academic competency.
